subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

CV Raman became famous when he got the Nobel Prize, __hadn't he?__
solution:
The correct answer is: **didn't he**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• We often use question tags when we expect the listener to agree with our statement. In this case, when the statement is positive, we use a negative question tag.
 
• Replace **"hadn't he?" **with **"didn’t he?"** to correct the sentence.
 
• “**Did**” is the past simple tense of the verb “**do**” which refers to performing an action. 
 
• "**Did he?**" is used here to refer back to the verb already mentioned. (got)
 
• “**had**” is the past participle tense of the verb “**have**” and it is only used in the past perfect tense.
 
• "**Was not**" is used as a helping verb to frame a negative sentence with I, he, she, it, any name or singular subject in the simple past tense when there is no verb in the given sentence.
 
• "**isn't**" is only used in the present tense and "**it**" refers to a non-living thing.
 
• Therefore, we should use "**didn't he?**" in the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

**Complete sentence:** *CV Raman became famous when he got the Nobel Prize, **didn't he?__***
